html:
Durable task dispatch and lifecycle projections

A durable task records accepted intent and its attempts. Native execution owns the actual work; traces, current-run views and notifications project its progress. Task storage describes the records and repositories. The conversation coordinator owns positioned chat tasks. This page follows the generic task-sheet/scheduled/workflow dispatch path in TaskService and its routes.

Accepting task-sheet intent

flowchart TD Request[POST generic task intent] --> License[Require current EULA acceptance] License --> Clean[Discard named internal admission<br/>and authority fields] Clean --> Capture[Capture supported controls,<br/>capability authority and read policies] Capture --> Target[Normalize Gateway intent<br/>and capture model routing] Target --> Parameters[Accept parameter references] Parameters --> Hold{Unresolved references and<br/>no conversation?} Hold -->|Yes| Conversation[Create conversation for clarification] Hold -->|No| Store[Create durable task] Conversation --> Store Store --> Usage[Record accepted parameter usage] Usage --> Start{start_now?} Start -->|No| Return[Return saved task projection] Start -->|Yes| Queue[Queue or start through TaskService] Queue --> Return

create_agent_task accepts generic task-sheet intent. It rejects a request trying to identify itself as a positioned composer task; the composer uses its dedicated conversation endpoint. The route removes named internal admission/runtime fields, normalizes supported settings and resolves capability authority through its owner. It captures supported Task Contract, context/read/recovery, redaction, behavior, execution and carry-forward values, Gateway intent and model routing. This is a series of owner reads, not one transaction that freezes every installation setting. Ordinary request admission still validates the eventual execution.

Parameter references are accepted before task creation. Missing references can create a durable clarification hold, with a conversation created when needed to present it. Usage accounting follows the admission owner's rules. A saved task or start_now request does not itself prove that a model call occurred. No macro parser runs in this route; see the separate retained macro integrations.

Permission/capability handling remains with the accepted context and admission owners. The generic dispatcher forwards retained permission policy explicitly for scheduled/workflow sources; this does not make every generic task a frozen copy of all effective global permissions.

Capacity, queue lanes and model turns

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Queue/start caller participant Service as TaskService participant Tasks as Durable task store participant Turns as Native AgentTurns participant Owners as Execution ownership Caller->>Service: Queue task under queue lock Service->>Tasks: Publish queued intent and inspect earlier eligible work Service->>Owners: Count live foreground execution owners alt Eight foreground owners already resident Service-->>Caller: Keep task queued else Dispatch-owner ceiling permits work Service->>Turns: Recover dead ownership and inspect leases/phases Turns-->>Service: Active calls, waiters and request phases Service->>Service: Count startup/unknown phases conservatively alt No configured Agent slot or nondefault lane is occupied Service-->>Caller: Keep task queued else Capacity available Service->>Tasks: Select earliest dependency-eligible task Service->>Service: Start accepted intent through ordinary admission Service-->>Caller: This task and any started-task metadata end end Note over Service,Turns: Logical tasks may remain open during detached waits<br/>Each later model call still acquires its own turn lease

The configured Agent parallel limit is clamped to 1–8. observed_capacity combines open task requests and tracked non-task requests with actual AgentTurns leases/phases. Active leases count; dispatch-reserved, ready and running phases count; an unknown phase is treated conservatively as startup work. A background wait can therefore release capacity while its logical task remains open. Turn counts and waiting counts remain separate from the task's status.

_available_run_slots also enforces an independent ceiling of eight live foreground execution owners. RAM checks the current hub generation; the standalone SQL path uses owner liveness. An already open/tracked request may resume deterministic reconciliation without a new generic slot, but subsequent model calls still require their own leases. See scheduling for model/Activity admission.

The generic queue lock protects selection/start coordination. The default lane fills available slots; another generic lane permits one open task and at most one start per fill pass. A chat: lane wakes the separate conversation coordinator and returns without using this dispatch loop. Selection respects explicit dependencies and queue/creation order; the eventual start rechecks dependencies. RAM selection also excludes Gateway-update holds through its store owner.

_queue_or_start_task returns already open work unchanged. Otherwise it publishes queued intent and a pending-run view, clears retry/resume previews when applicable, and lets earlier eligible tasks run first. The response may describe other tasks started during that fill pass as well as the requested task.

Starting an attempt and surviving a failed response

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Dispatch caller participant Service as TaskService participant Gates as Admission gates participant History as Task/attempt history participant Request as Request submission participant Native as Native state and trace participant Monitor as Monitor Caller->>Service: Start accepted task Service->>Gates: Check holds, dependencies,<br/>EULA, archive and availability alt Unresolved parameter hold Service-->>Caller: Return held task without dispatch else Required gate prevents start Service->>History: Reject or project interrupted/skipped outcome as applicable else Start permitted Service->>History: Create running attempt and prepare task context Service->>Request: Submit captured intent<br/>and optional prepared identity alt Submission returns a request Request-->>Service: Request/conversation identity Service->>History: Bind attempt, task and occurrence Service->>Native: Publish current-run and start metadata Service->>Monitor: Observe returned request else Submission raises after a prepared trace exists Service->>Native: Inspect retained execution and diagnostic Service->>History: Reconcile the same identity into task/occurrence views opt Retained execution is still open Service->>Monitor: Keep observing without relaunching end Service-->>Caller: Propagate original failure else Submission raises without a retained prepared trace Service->>History: Mark attempt/task failed and project occurrence/notification Service->>Service: Reconsider queued work Service-->>Caller: Propagate original failure end end

_start_task_now returns unresolved parameter holds before starting an attempt. It records usage through the admission owner, checks dependencies, requires EULA acceptance, rejects archived work and runs availability preflight. Missing acceptance projects interruption and, for an occurrence, a skipped result. Unavailable Agent resources similarly project interruption/skipping and applicable notifications. These paths are distinct from a model that ran and failed.

After the gates, the service creates an attempt and copies accepted context with task/attempt/occurrence identities. Retained requirements may cause the existing terminal owner to attach a background session. The ordinary submission helper receives captured policy, parameter and execution intent through its trusted internal arguments. A scheduled occurrence or workflow invocation can provide a prepared request identity, preserving correlation across admission failure.

The submission exception path checks that retained identity before deciding what happened. If admission failed before native work exists, it supplies a structured diagnostic to the prepared trace and projects the same failure into the task, attempt, occurrence and conversation views. If work was already dispatched, it keeps observing the existing execution rather than submitting it again. A lost or failed response is not evidence that execution never began.

These are separate owner operations. They are not a single transaction that rolls back every task, trace, event, notification or external effect. Monitoring and retained-trace reconciliation repair presentation state from existing evidence.

Monitoring, user-visible status and notifications

flowchart TD Trace[Retained native status and request trace] --> Status[Map native outcome to task lane status] Status --> Checkpoints[Append deduplicated task checkpoints] Checkpoints --> Run[Refresh current-run projection] Run --> Outcome{Task status beyond<br/>running/pending?} Outcome -->|No| Wait[Wait for events or bounded polling] Outcome -->|Yes| Settled{Transport settled?} Settled -->|No| Wait Wait --> Trace Settled -->|Yes| Final[Update attempt and task bindings/previews] Final --> Scheduled{Native model-led<br/>scheduled event?} Scheduled -->|Yes| Delivery[Leave notification policy<br/>with the event owner] Scheduled -->|No| Notice[Create deduplicated task notification] Delivery --> Event[Update linked occurrence when present] Notice --> Event Event --> Continue[Reconsider default queue after<br/>non-interaction outcomes] Final --> Projection[Task API view: timing, purge deadline,<br/>model routes, dependencies and user action]

One task-attempt monitor is registered per request. It copies new trace events to task checkpoints, refreshes the run view and waits for the transport to settle before finalizing previews and notifications. Native completion can precede the final transport response. Conversely, paused/partial native work can outlive a completed transport; bounded polling avoids spinning on its terminal trace. The monitor removes its registration on every exit and observes the shutdown signal.

Task status is an operational projection. Scheduled partial/blocked outcomes map to interrupted so dispatch capacity can be released. Resource reconciliation maps to a clarification lane wait, while the native outcome remains distinct. Missing trace evidence remains conservatively running. Retained-trace reconciliation does not reopen an already terminal task merely because an older trace looks open.

Non-task tracking follows pending continuation chains with cycle protection. Its pending predicate treats statuses other than completed/failed/cancelled as pending, including interrupted. Completed confirmation/clarification waits remain pending until handled. Its monitor records tracking failures, retries up to three errors and releases the root tracking entry on exit; that bookkeeping release does not cancel external execution.

Checkpoint detail attempts debug redaction before JSON serialization and bounds oversized text. If that redactor raises, this helper falls back to the original detail, so it is not an unconditional secret-removal guarantee. Checkpoints remain task-owned projections of trace events, not substitutes for native evidence.

Notifications are deduplicated by task, attempt/request and status. Running status does not create one. Native model-led scheduled events retain their event owner's notification policy, avoiding a second task notification. Action-error metadata can change severity/body even when the task completed; clipboard diagnostics use generic notification text. Notification creation does not establish successful delivery.

Task views add timing, observed purge deadlines, actual model routes from retained traces, latest checkpoints, required user action and scheduled-source availability. Dependency display includes bounded same-conversation predecessor metadata without recursively expanding the graph. Generic task listing can reconcile history and best-effort advance the queue; it is not a purely passive read. Status counts are drawn from a separate sample of at most 500 rows, not an unlimited repository total.

Cancellation races and continuation attempts

sequenceDiagram participant User as Task control caller participant Service as TaskService participant Owner as Admission / chat / native owner participant History as Task and attempt history User->>Service: Cancel task alt Unstarted parameter-admission hold Service->>Owner: Revision-checked hold cancellation else Positioned chat task Service->>Owner: Remove queued intent or cancel current request Service->>Owner: Wake and reconcile conversation lane else Generic task Service->>History: Reconcile retained terminal outcome first alt Completion/failure already won Service-->>User: Preserve that outcome and reconsider queue else Work remains open Service->>Owner: Request native cancellation Service->>History: Project cancellation if terminal outcome did not win Service->>History: Update occurrence and applicable notification end end Note over User,History: Separate continuation operation, not a cancellation step opt Caller supplies an existing follow-up request identity User->>Service: Bind supplied child request to this task Service->>History: Create child attempt linked to parent request Service->>History: Rebind task/current-run/occurrence and monitor child end

Native cancellation is preferred. The compatibility fallback sets a local cancel signal and schedules best-effort Gateway command cancellation, then updates retained trace/current-run/conversation views when present. Gateway cancellation failures are suppressed in that fallback. A cancelled task projection therefore cannot guarantee that a remote process stopped or that an effect was reversed.

Generic cancellation first reconciles retained evidence and preserves a completion or failure that won the race. Parameter holds and positioned chat tasks use their own owners. A follow-up request creates a distinct attempt linked to its parent and updates the task/occurrence bindings before monitoring the child; it is not a retry of an unknown external effect.

Archive, deletion and retained ownership

flowchart TD Control[Archive, retry or delete request] --> Chat{Positioned chat task?} Chat -->|Yes| Lane[Retry/delete through conversation controls<br/>Generic archive is rejected] Chat -->|No| Generic[Apply generic task control rules] Generic --> Retry[Retry requires inactive work<br/>and creates a new attempt] Generic --> Archive[Cancel open work, then mark archived] Generic --> Delete[Collect model owners and<br/>delete task-owned rows through store guards] Delete --> Guards[Preserve referenced predecessors,<br/>pending steers and protected intent] Guards --> Removed[Remove task, attempts/checkpoints<br/>and owned dependency bookkeeping] Removed --> Revoke[Revoke collected model-call owners] Native[Native journals, effects and scratch state] --> Lifecycle[Remain with their own<br/>retention/deletion owners]

Generic start/retry requires EULA acceptance. Start accepts queued, interrupted, failed or cancelled states; retry rejects open generic work and clears outcome previews for its new attempt. Positioned chat tasks use the conversation coordinator's retry/control rules; the generic archive route rejects positioned chat tasks. Archive cancels open generic work before marking its history archived.

Generic deletion removes task-owned rows through SQL or RAM retention/dependency guards. The route collects current/latest requests and retained attempt-owned model leases before deletion, then revokes them after successful removal. A batch skips open task states; store guards still protect referenced predecessors, pending amendments and blocking chat intent. Native RunStore history and external effects are outside this generic task-store operation.

Conversation task retirement and asynchronous cleanup have a separate boundary; see deletion feedback and cleanup. A history row being absent is not proof that every underlying file or remote effect disappeared.

Verification and limits

Scheduled-submission fixtures exercise captured intent, one scripted execution, startup failures and restart projection without duplicating the occurrence. The focused Agent-turn capacity case checks that background waits release API capacity while tasks remain open. Selected runtime-issue and capability-scope cases cover parameter holds and task-sheet authority capture. These use scripted model responses and fixture stores/transports; the scheduled execution performs an isolated uname -s check. They do not exercise a live model/provider or production Gateway.
